methods.label: Simplify the new roots to negative reciprocals
methods.explanation:
The missing cubic term tells us the sum of the original roots. To see why, write the original variable as \(t\) and factor using the four roots, counted with multiplicity:
\[
t^4-bt-3=(t-a)(t-b)(t-c)(t-d).
\]
A cubic term in this product comes from choosing a constant from one factor and \(t\) from the other three. Its coefficient is therefore \(-(a+b+c+d)\). Comparing with the zero cubic coefficient gives
\[
a+b+c+d=0.
\]
Also, none of these roots is zero, since the original polynomial has value \(-3\) at zero. All displayed denominators are consequently nonzero.

Each new expression now simplifies in the same way; for example,
\[
\frac{a+b+c}{d^2}=\frac{-d}{d^2}=-\frac1d.
\]
Thus the requested roots are \(-1/d,-1/c,-1/b,-1/a\).

If \(t\) is an original root, put \(y=-1/t\), so \(t=-1/y\) and \(y\ne0\). Substituting into the original equation gives
\[
\frac1{y^4}+\frac b y-3=0.
\]
Multiplying by the nonzero number \(y^4\) and rearranging yields
\[
3y^4-by^3-1=0.
\]
Conversely, this new polynomial has no zero root, and reversing the substitution sends every one of its roots back to an original root. The correspondence also retains any repeated roots. Renaming \(y\) as \(x\), the required equation is
\[
\boxed{3x^4-bx^3-1=0},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
